title: Nobel Peace Prize 2026 goes to Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law
summary: South African judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay has won this year's Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law. Follow DW live.

image.caption: Chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee Jorgen Watne Frydnes speaking at the Peace Prize ceremony last year [FILE December 2025]Image: Stian Lysberg Solum/NTB/REUTERS

items: Navanethem "Navi" Pillay has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
The Peace Prize committee is the only one that regularly recognizes achievements from the previous year
It has been awarded 106 times to 143 laureates between 1901 and 2025
The prize carries a cash award of 12 million Swedish kronor (around $1.2 million; €1 million)
This week, Nobel laureates have already been named in medicine, physics, chemistry, and literature.

blocks.text: Below is all the news and views, previews and reviews surrounding the award of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.
Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Navi Pillay
South African human rights lawyer Navanethem "Navi" Pillay has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

Born in 1941 in Durban, Pillay grew up under apartheid and became one of South Africa's first women of Indian descent to practice law. She defended anti-apartheid activists and fought against discriminatory prison conditions.

After apartheid, she became a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, where she helped establish landmark legal precedents recognizing rape as an act of genocide. She later served as a judge at the International Criminal Court and as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014.
More recently, she chaired a UN commission investigating human rights violations in Israel and the Palestinian territories.
